svg.title: Guidance can redistribute directional performance without uniformly improving control
svg.desc: Two DROID model panels compare baseline and guidance intervention success counts, exact-seed requested endpoint margins, and the mean RIGHT-minus-LEFT margin gap. A smaller gap is not interpreted as improved balance when both margins fall.

g.text: V2-A015 exploratory DROID/RoboLab ablation · same reset, task predicate, static prompt, and seeds 8300–8302 within each model
“Put the Rubik's cube to the left of the bowl.”
“Put the Rubik's cube to the right of the bowl.”
filled = full task success · hollow = failure
Joint action–video guidance reduced: g = 3 baseline → g = 1 (no joint CFG blend)
Observed: mean-margin gap narrowed because RIGHT fell more; total success 6/6 → 4/6.
n = 3 matched seeds per direction and setting
RIGHT mean − LEFT mean; sign identifies the larger margin
Observed: mean-margin gap narrowed because RIGHT fell more; total success 6/6 → 4/6.

g.text: Requested endpoint margin (m) · positive is farther into the requested side
LEFT uses −final lateral coordinate; RIGHT uses +final lateral coordinate. Positive means the endpoint lies on the requested side.
A positive endpoint margin is not automatically a success; the full task also requires the official release-inside-45°-cone predicate.
Post-result descriptive pilot: three matched seeds per direction and setting. Raw counts and paired effects are shown without CI, p-value, or powered significance claim.
s=2 is derived CFG-style negative-branch action guidance using the released visual-quality negative prompt—not an official action-CFG feature. DROID only; no RoboTwin pooling.
